findings.title: Future-dated summary freezes session counters
findings.problem: The SESSION recompute picks the latest agent.session.summary by the client's own timestamp (the sm lateral, ORDER BY h.ts DESC, lines 924-928), and _SUMMARY_WINS (line 841) accepts a summary only when its ts is not older than the stored summary_ts. Nothing bounds that timestamp: a summary dated in the future (a client clock error) becomes the stored summary_ts, and every later, correctly dated summary is older and is ignored until real time passes that date. The identity and story pairs compare identity_ts / story_ts in the same way. The session purge in maintenance.py already treats a client time after today as a clock error (_past); the summary merge does not.
findings.impact: One wrongly dated summary leaves the session's summary columns (turns, tool and line counts, commands, title, ended_at, duration_ms) at that event's values for as long as its date lies ahead; with a far-future date that is permanent, because the row keeps summary_ts after the raw event is gone. The effect is limited to the session the event names. Confirmed against the source: hook_events.ts is the event's own time on both routes.
findings.recommendation: Decide and record one of: (a) when choosing the latest summary, identity and story event, ignore an event whose ts lies after today, the rule _past applies in the purge - with the same bound in the sm lateral and in _SUMMARY_WINS so that incremental and full recalculation agree; or (b) list the behaviour in spec section 7 as a known limitation. The spec sections handed to this review do not show it recorded, which is why this is a decision and not a patch.

findings.title: Subagent duration can be stored negative
findings.problem: subagent_invocations.duration_ms falls back to _ms_between('tm.ended_at', 'tm.started_at') (lines 1302-1306) when the usage event carries no duration_ms. tm.started_at and tm.ended_at (lines 1394-1397) come from different client-dated sources - the usage event's started_at / ended_at, else the first start event, the latest stop event, or the earliest request - and nothing checks that the end is not before the start.
findings.impact: When the chosen end precedes the chosen start (clock skew between events, a usage event that carries only started_at after an earlier stop, a malformed pair), a negative duration is written to a long-term table whose other client numbers are all read as non-negative (_json_count, _whole_number). No endpoint reads the table yet (spec section 10), so today the effect is stored data only; a later sum or average over duration_ms would be wrong.
findings.recommendation: Write the computed fallback only when tm.ended_at >= tm.started_at, else NULL, so the NULL rule keeps a stored value: wrap the _ms_between term in CASE WHEN tm.ended_at >= tm.started_at THEN ... END inside the coalesce. Pin the guard in test_rollups.py as the other bounds are pinned.

findings.title: Removed engine still named in code
findings.problem: AC12 requires that nothing in the code mentions ClickHouse, the Collector or their settings. Still present at HEAD: the test name test_doubles_render_like_the_collector (test_otlp.py:107); the comment 'the reader may return Decimal / None / UInt64 variously' at src/codemie/service/analytics/handlers/cli_analytics_handler.py:62, a ClickHouse type name; and the module docstring line 'The hook constants define the hook types and attribute keys the router forwards' at src/codemie/repository/cli_analytics/vocabulary.py:24, which describes forwarding to the Collector (reported as stale: the change deletes HOOK_ATTRIBUTE_KEYS and the router forwards nothing - confirm while editing). test_otlp.py:528 (..._like_the_router_forwards_them) has the same wording. The spec's own grep (clickhouse|otelcollector|ANALYTICS_INGEST_OTLP) matches none of these spellings, so it passes. Not part of this finding: CLI_ANALYTICS_STORAGE_BACKEND in test_config_cli_analytics.py:41 and test_factory.py:41 asserts that the setting is gone, and ch_uint / ch_float are out of scope by spec section 6.
findings.impact: The acceptance row AC12 stays partial: the story's wording is not met although its grep check passes, and the leftovers describe an engine a reader can no longer find in the tree. No runtime effect.
findings.recommendation: Rename the test after what it checks (for example the shortest decimal form of a double), and reword the two comments in terms of the PostgreSQL reader and the current router. Optionally widen the spec's grep with 'collector' so the check covers the criterion's wording.

findings.title: Added test functions lack type annotations
findings.problem: code-quality.md:18 lists 'Untyped public functions in new code' under Avoid and prefers explicit parameter and return types. 107 of the 216 functions this range adds under tests/ have no return annotation, and some leave parameters unannotated, across 12 existing test modules: test_otlp.py (33 of 35, e.g. :528, :819, :848), tests/codemie/rest_api/routers/test_cli_analytics_ingest.py (23 of 29, e.g. :133, :141), test_dirty.py (13 of 27, e.g. :130 '_hooks(*events)'), test_migrations.py (10 of 13), test_reader.py (9 of 11, e.g. :528 'capture(sql, params)'), test_ingestor.py (6 of 8), test_maintenance.py (3 of 14, e.g. :253), test_rollups.py (2 of 39), tests/codemie/repository/cli_analytics/test_factory.py (4 of 4), tests/codemie/service/analytics/test_cli_analytics_jobs.py (2 of 2), test_backfill.py:268 and tests/codemie/configs/test_config_cli_analytics.py:39. The three new test modules of the same change are fully annotated.
findings.impact: The code-quality standards row is partial, which blocks the gate. Ruff selects no annotation rule, so no automated gate catches it; the older tests in the same files are mostly unannotated as well, so the change follows the files' habit and not the guide, which states no exemption for tests.
findings.recommendation: Add '-> None' (or the real return type) and parameter types to the functions and helpers this range adds. If tests are meant to be exempt, record that exemption in .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md instead, so the rule and the practice agree.

findings.title: Bare dict annotation in added test helper
findings.problem: code-quality.md:19 lists bare list/dict annotations under Avoid and prefers parameterized generics. The added helper '_decode_logs(event: dict, record_ts: datetime | None = RECORD_T)' annotates event as a bare dict and has no return annotation.
findings.impact: Part of the same partial code-quality standards row; the line is introduced by this range and Ruff does not check it.
findings.recommendation: Annotate the parameter with a parameterized type such as dict[str, object] and add the return type.
